summary: Isaiah-as-seer short is KJV-verbatim clean, narratively grounded in Isa 52:13-53:12 + Acts 8, and lands soundly and grace-anchored on the substitutionary atonement of Jesus.

findings.quote_or_claim: a stranger read my words aloud and asked the very question I had asked: of whom speaketh the prophet this?
findings.problem: The question 'of whom speaketh the prophet this?' is the Ethiopian eunuch's (Acts 8:34), not a question Isaiah is recorded asking. Attributing it as 'the very question I had asked' is a poetic identification. It is defensible (Isa 53:1 'Who hath believed our report?'; 1 Pet 1:10-11 the prophets inquired) and the words themselves are verbatim KJV, so it is a creative flourish rather than a fact-inversion; noted for transparency only and does not change the verdict.
findings.proposed_fix_text: a stranger read my words aloud and asked aloud the question my own report had always raised: of whom speaketh the prophet this?
